ORAL JUDGMENT Heard Sri.Ganesh R., learned counsel for the appellant as well as Sri.Sharanappa Gouda, learned counsel for respondent No.2.
2.
Seeking enhancement of compensation, this appeal is filed by the claimant disputing the order that is passed by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Udupi in MVC.No.556/2018 dated 07.11.2020.

As against the claim for Rs.7,95,000/- the Tribunal awarded a sum of NC:
2024:KHC:32436 Rs.4,37,078/- as compensation and aggrieved by the same, the claimant is before this Court.
3. Sri.Ganesh R., learned counsel for the appellant arguing the matter contends that the appellant sustained four injuries due to the accident and became permanently disabled.
Learned counsel also states that the appellant was an employee at Dubai by the date of accident and he was earning more than Rs.30,000/- per month.
Sufficient proof was produced before the Tribunal to establish the occupation and earnings of the appellant by the date of accident.
More particularly, Ex.P18 reveal the credit of salary and the other transactions.

However, without considering the said evidence, the Tribunal taking notional income as Rs.25,000/- per month, awarded very meager amount under the head 'loss of future earnings', which is unjustifiable.

Learned counsel also states that the Tribunal without taking into account the nature of the injuries sustained by the appellant, the inconvenience faced and the allied aspects, awarded meager sum as compensation NC: 2024:KHC:32436 under all heads and therefore, this Court is liable to interfere.
4.

On the other hand, the submission that is made by Sri.Sharanappa Gouda, learned counsel for respondent No.2 is that the appellant failed to produce any cogent and convincing proof with regard to his actual occupation and income by the date of accident.

Learned counsel also states that out of the four injuries sustained by the appellant, three are simple in nature and only one is grievous in Abdul Rehaman Mohammed vs M Krishnappa on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6095074/
2 nature.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel also states that the appellant continued his job after recovery and thus,
there is no 'loss of future earning' as such.
Learned counsel further submits that as the amount awarded as compensation is just and reasonable, the appeal is not maintainable.

5. A perusal of record reveals that the Tribunal assessed and awarded compensation under following heads:
NC: 2024:KHC:32436 Sl. Heads Calculation No. i. Medical expenses relating to Rs.71,078/-
 treatment and hospitalization  and medicines  ii. Pain and suffering Rs.40,000/-
 iii. Loss of income during the Rs.50,000/-
 treatment period  iv. Loss of future earning capacity Rs.2,43,000/-
 due to permanent disability  v. Conveyance Charges Rs.3,000/-
 vi. Food, nourishment, attendant Rs.5,000/-
 charges  vii. Loss of amenities Rs.10,000/-
 viii. Future medical expenses Rs.15,000/-
 Total Rs.4,37,078/-
 6.
Undisputedly, the appellant sustained an abrasion on forehead, an abrasion on left eyebrow, a contusion on left side of chest and fracture of left humerus.
Apart from taking treatment for the fracture of the left humerus, it is clear that the appellant took treatment for the injury sustained to his left eye.
The NC: 2024:KHC:32436 evidence of PW.2 establishes the said fact.
Though by the contents of Ex.P18-Passbook, it is clear that certain amount was credited towards salary of the appellant time to time.
Yet the exact salary which the appellant was receiving monthly or fortnightly is not established in clear terms by the appellant.
Therefore, this Court is of the view that the notional income as assessed by the Tribunal i.e., Rs.25,000/- per month needs no interference.

However, having considered the 'pain and suffering' experienced by the appellant and the nature of treatment taken, this Court is of the view that the appellant could not have attended his normal pursuits at least for a period of three months.

sentences.text: Therefore, a sum of Rs.25,000/- is required to be granted additionally under the said head.
Likewise, having considered the nature of injuries sustained, this Court is of the view that an addition of Rs.10,000/- is required to be made for 'pain and suffering'.
The Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.3,000/- only towards 'conveyance charges'.

Having considered the NC: 2024:KHC:32436 fact that the appellant took treatment for the injuries sustained to the eye as well as fracture to the humerus, this Court is of the view that an addition of Rs.10,000/- is required to be made under 'conveyance charges'.
Likewise, the amount awarded under the head 'food, nourishment and attendance charges' i.e., Rs.5,000/- is liable to be increased by another sum of Rs.20,000/-.
The Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/- only towards 'loss of amenities'.
However, a sum of Rs.10,000/- is liable to be increased under the said head.
Therefore, the enhancement in compensation would be to an extent of Rs.75,000/- in total.

Thus, in the light of the foregoing discussion, the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.
ii) The amount that is awarded as compensation by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Udupi through orders in MVC.No.556/2018 dated 07.11.2020 is enhanced by Rs.75,000/-.
NC: 2024:KHC:32436 iii) The enhanced amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
iv) Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the enhanced amount within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
v) On such deposit, the appellant is permitted to withdraw the entire amount.

Sd/-
(DR.CHILLAKUR SUMALATHA) JUDGE NR/-
